rfis.question: There is conflicting information regarding the requirement for Filed Sub-bids. Section 00 11 13 and Section 00 41 13 state they are not required, while Section 00 12 13 states they are required. Please clarify if Filed Sub-bids are required for this project. If so, please provide the due date for Filed Sub-bids, as it is currently left blank in Section 00 12 13.
rfis.answer: Filed sub bids are not required

rfis.question: Please clarify if Pre-qualified General Contractors are utilized for this project. Section 00 11 13 indicates they are utilized but does not list names, while Section 00 12 13 states there are none.
rfis.answer: Prequalified subcontractors are not utilized

rfis.question: Please provide an electrical allowance for bidding purposes, as it is difficult for contractors to accurately identify and quantify the electrical work required.
rfis.answer: We will carry a $3,000 dollar allowance for this.

rfis.question: Please confirm whether the Contractor is required to include temporary heating costs in the bid, as the anticipated completion date of December 30, 2026 may result in significant heating-related expenses.
rfis.answer: Contractor is required to provide heating as required to complete the repairs as needed in 2026. Contractor may be able to complete repairs without additional heat in spring 2027.

rfis.question: Is there any reason the project would not be able to start in the Spring 2027, when 14 York Street, Suite 201 | Portland ME 04101 - 7408 | T 207.245.6060 | F | www.ThorntonTomasetti.com RFI Response BGS Project 2995 Capital Parking Garage 2026 Repairs September 18, 2026, Page 2 weather conditions would be more favorable for performing the work?
rfis.answer: We would prefer to have a start date this fall and can extend the finish date to Spring 2027, June 18, 2027.

rfis.question: Please confirm the designated location(s) for material storage and dumpster staging during construction.
rfis.answer: This will be coordinated during the preconstruction meeting.

rfis.question: For Bid Item 3- Supplemental Steel Beam- Please confirm that the North side of the garage will get 3ea of the supplemental beams and south side will get 4ea of the supplemental beams. In sheet S1.5, the North side only shows two beams.
rfis.answer: That is correct. There are 7 beams total. 4 beams on the north and 3 on the south side of the parking structure. There is a partial plan for the portion of the ramp that extends from gridlines 13- 14 that is included on sheet S1.5.

rfis.question: For Item 16- Wall repairs- please provide repair detail.
rfis.answer: Repair details are 6 and 7 / S2.2

rfis.question: Please provide available as-built drawings for the garage.
rfis.answer: We have electronic copies and can provide.

rfis.question: Please confirm whether water will be available for the Contractor's use on site.
rfis.answer: Water is on site and available for contractor use. However, the meter is typically removed at the start of winter to prevent freezing and reinstalled in the spring.

rfis.question: Please confirm whether power and functioning electrical outlets will be available for the Contractor's use on site.
rfis.answer: Functional outlets are located in the stairwells, however, all receptacles have limited capacity and should not be counted on for running heavy grinders or electric chipping guns.

rfis.question: Please confirm the maximum number of parking stalls that may be closed at any one time and identify any required work area enclosures, barriers, or other protection measures that must be maintained during construction.
rfis.answer: 25 Spaces are allowed for your use. These spaces do not include the top deck while it remains closed until the post tensioning repairs are completed.

rfis.question: Please confirm that the bid due date and time is September 25, 2026, at 1:30 PM, as there appears to be conflicting information regarding the bid opening date within the contract documents.
rfis.answer: The bid due date is September 30, 2026 at 1:30 PM. The bids will be opened at 2:00 PM.

rfis.question: Please confirm if contractor is responsible for obtaining permits required for this project.
rfis.answer: Contractor is responsible for obtaining any required permits.

rfis.question: Please confirm if contractor is responsible for paying any permit fees required for this project. RFI Response BGS Project 2995 Capital Parking Garage 2026 Repairs September 18, 2026, Page 4
rfis.answer: Contractor is responsible for permit fees.

rfis.question: Please confirm whether this project is exempt from sales tax and whether bids should be submitted on a tax-exempt basis.
rfis.answer: Yes, this project is exempt from sales tax. BGS will issue the required paperwork to the selected contractor.

rfis.question: Please confirm whether the project is to be bid using open shop labor rates.
rfis.answer: Please use the Kennebec County Prevailing wages.

rfis.question: For Waterproofing Membrane repairs- A 5 year warranty may not be available from the manufacturer for localized installations and repairs, which is the scope for this project. Please confirm that the warranty duration and terms made available by the manufacturer will be acceptable even if they are different than what is included in the current bid documents.
rfis.answer: A 5 year warranty is not required for repair areas.

rfis.question: Are Liquidated Damages required for this project.
rfis.answer: Liquidated damages are included in this project. Please see the requirements in Section 00 72 13 General Conditions added to the addendum.

rfis.question: Per SECTION 00 51 01 – Phase I Evaluation, page 38 of the RFP, the overall proposal is limited to a maximum of 50 pages. This constraint is restrictive due to the extensive volume of mandatory forms, certifications, and disclosures required by the CDB for the Phase I submission. These administrative requirements consume a substantial portion of the total page allotment, leaving insufficient space for offerors to provide comprehensive technical narratives, detailed experience, and qualifications necessary to best respond to the RFP. We request that the CDB waive this overall 50-page limit.
rfis.answer: There are no page limits for section 1. Sections 2, 3 and 4 have a combined page limit of 50 pages. Section 2 has a 25-page limit but the Past Performance Evaluation Questionnaires (PPEQ) and MBE/WBE/VBE/PBE Phase I Utilization Plan do not count against the 25 pages. Section 3 has a 12- page total limit with a 5-page limit for technical capacity, 5-page limit for team experience narrative and 2-page limit for other capability information.

rfis.question: Per SECTION 00 42 10 – Submission Requirements and Instructions, page 16 of the RFP, Section 2 (Experience and Qualifications) is currently limited to 25 pages. This constraint is insufficient to adequately address the evaluation criteria for both “Experience of Personnel Assigned to the Project” and "Past Performance" while also fulfilling the requirement to include all necessary resumes and documents within the Design-Build Entity Qualifications Form (DBQ). We request that the CDB either waive this 25-page limit or increase the page allotment in this section to 50 pages.
rfis.answer: Section 2 has a 25-page limit but the Past Performance Evaluation Questionnaires (PPEQ) and MBE/WBE/VBE/PBE Phase I Utilization Plan do not count against the 25 pages.

rfis.question: Please confirm whether or not resumes are to be included in the 25 page limit for Section 2 Past Performance (pg.16). If so, may additional resumes be included in an appendix?
rfis.answer: Resumes should be listed in the Design-Build Entity Qualifications Form (DBQ), which count against the 25-page limit for Section 2. Any appendix in this section would count towards your 25-page limit.

rfis.question: Please provide additional information on the existing single story building on the north side of the property that is to be demolished as part of this project. - Architectural and Structural as-builts - Utility connections/survey - Hazardous material survey
rfis.answer: The documents have been shared.

rfis.question: The plat of survey provided in the bridging document does not indicate any campus utility tunnels or the location of campus chilled water and steam lines. Can this survey be provided?
rfis.answer: The CAD and pdf file of campus utilities have been shared.

rfis.question: Can this source document used as the background for proposed work in exhibit 2 be provided?
rfis.answer: The source document will be provided via Amendment 3.

rfis.question: Section 8.4 of the bridging documents indicates the building will be supplied by a campus fire line. The bridging documents indicate a fire pump is expected for the building. Was a water supply flow test data obtained? If yes, can it be provided?
rfis.answer: No recent flow test data was provided or obtained.

rfis.question: The proposed new electrical ductbank exhibit 8 indicate quantities and cross section of proposed ductbanks. The cross sections show a maximum of (4) rows for conduits. Does this (4) row limitation mimic existing ductbank configuration or is there source material that can be shared with the team identifying the existing ductbank cross section and buried depths?
rfis.answer: Confirmed. The (4) row conduit duct bank section mimics the existing duct bank configuration.

rfis.question: In section 8.2 of the bridging document, the building will be supplied with a new high pressure steam pipe and condensate line from building 921 (campus steam plant) via the utility bridge over Taylor street. Confirm the contractor will be responsible for all of the piping as well as supplemental structural support for the Taylor street utility bridge. When entering the building 921, will the contractor be responsible for the existing building penetration and modifications to any piping manifolds or infrastructure to tap into existing steam and condensate lines? What will UIC facilities be responsible for the supply of steam/condensate to this building such as any equipment additions to the plant to support this building or supply of any metering equipment?
rfis.answer: a. The Contractor shall be responsible for all piping and supplemental structural supports per the Bridging Documents. b. An enabling project will be conducted by UIC and provide taps and isolation valves for high pressure steam and steam condensate piping that this Contractor will connect outside of Building

rfis.question: In section 8.2 of the bridging document, the building will be supplied with a new chilled water supply and return line from building 952 (campus refrigeration plant) via the utility bridge over Taylor street and the UIC Hospital loading dock. Confirm the contractor will be responsible for all of the piping as well as supplemental structural support for the Taylor street utility bridge and supplemental structural support for UIC Hospital loading dock roof. When entering the building 952, will the contractor be responsible for the existing building penetration and modifications to any piping manifolds or infrastructure to tap into existing steam and condensate lines? What will UIC facilities be responsible for the supply of steam/condensate to this building such as any equipment additions to the plant to support this building or supply of any metering equipment?
rfis.answer: a. The Contractor shall be responsible for all piping and supplemental structural supports per the Bridging Documents. b. An enabling project will be conducted by UIC and provide taps and isolation valves for high pressure steam and steam condensate piping that this Contractor will connect outside of Building

rfis.question: Please provide UIC Hospital structural drawings, in particular those relevant to the loading dock for reference.
rfis.answer: Hospital drawings will not be shared. Please indicate if there are specific pieces of information needed from those drawings and UIC may be able to provide.

rfis.question: Section 8.2 of the bridging document indicates process cooling system will originate from the campus refrigeration plant. This section also indicates local water-cooled chillers with cooling towers are required since the campus chilled water system is not available year-round. Confirm the campus cooling chilled water system is not available year-round and local cooling equipment is needed at the building to maintain process cooling system.
rfis.answer: Per UIC, we can confirm that winter/swing-season cooling will be available for DDCRP at the start of the project. Cooling will be available year-round from UIC utilities.

rfis.question: Confirm campus steam system will be available year-round or if local equipment is needed at the building.
rfis.answer: Yes, steam will be available all year round. No local steam generators will be needed.

rfis.question: The Bridging Documents (page 279 for example) make reference to the Clients insurance recommendations for sprinkler design densities. Please confirm there are no additional Client Insurance requirements (such as FM Global), for any systems, beyond explicit performance and code requirements outlined in the Bridging Documents.
rfis.answer: UIC does not follow FM Global guidelines; the system should be designed to the latest edition of NFPA 13.

rfis.question: The Bridging Documents identify Preaction and Clean Agent Sprinkler Systems but do not outline where these are required. Please confirm these systems are not required as they are not normally provided in a Research Lab.
rfis.answer: Some research laboratories do have dry/preaction requirements. Those systems descriptions are present in the Bridging Documents in the event that the owner decides that they are appropriate for certain areas. Additionally, if there are areas subject to freezing in the final design, dry systems are to be implemented.

rfis.question: Ref: BOD - pg 524 Please confirm that the trash/recycling compactors and waste dumpsters will be provided by the Owner.
rfis.answer: Trash/recycling compactors and waste dumpsters, including biowaste containers, for the building's loading dock are to be included in the Design-Build team's budget (not owner-provided). Some additional details on the components described in Section 2.2 Space Program Tabulation (page 25) and Section 9.3 Loading Dock (page 524) of the Bridging Documents are as follows:

rfis.question: Ref: BOD - pg 470 There is reference to a UIC irrigation contractor, Aquamist in the Bridging Documents. Please confirm that the owner is to carry costs for this irrigation contractor, including irrigation system design, and the irrigation scope is not to be included in the total amount.
rfis.answer: Irrigation is to be included in the design build scope of work.

rfis.question: Ref: RFP - pg 8, Design-Build Pricing Schedule Section 00 21 40 of the RFP notes that "Offerers shall include an allowance for the CAF assessment in their Phase II cost proposal". The Pricing Schedule notes "CONTRACT ADMINISTRATION FEE is not included in the DBPS but will still be applied to the project". Please confirm that the contract administration fee (CAF) is NOT to be included in the total amount.
rfis.answer: Amendment 3 addresses this.

rfis.question: Ref: BOD - pg 1260 Advise if hazardous materials (e.g. lead paint, asbestos, etc) are present in Pharmacy Building 521.
rfis.answer: Refer to Limited Asbestos-Containing Material and Lead-Based Paint Building Survey Report the Pharmacy Building (available in Bridging Documents Section 13.5b Building Environmental Report). Per this report: a. "Lead-Based Paint was not identified on any of the painted surfaces/components tested during this limited survey," but "'negative readings'...should not be interpreted as lead is not present" and "surfaces/components...not assessed during this survey...shall be assumed and treated as LBP until tested and proven otherwise." b. "The...[Asbestos-Containing Material]...identified during this limited survey included the black wall mastic that was identified throughout the 3rd and 4th floor corridors above 2' x 2' ceiling tile," but "Any suspect material that is discovered during the renovation / demolition activities and is not listed in Table 3.1...shall be assumed and treated as ACUM until tested and proven otherwise."

rfis.question: The "Supplement to the SD-DB 3.2017" was issued by the CDB in the RFP and referenced in section 00 21 15 of the Request for Proposals. Please advise if the "Supplement to design build sdc 1.2025" located on in the CDB reference library should be used instead.
rfis.answer: Supplement to Design Build SDC 1.2025 will be required. Amendment 3 addresses this form.

rfis.question: Ref: ORP page 5 As a state funded facility, the UIC DDCRP is required to comply with the 2023 Illinois Stretch Energy Code per the Energy Efficiency Building Act (20 ILCS 3125), which went into effect on January 1, 2025.Our code analysis shows that the DDCRP cannot comply with the 2023 Illinois Stretch Energy Code if thermal utilities are provided through steam and chilled water connections to the existing West Campus central plant, as described in the Bridging Documents. Please confirm that a variance will be provided to relieve the project from complying with the 2023 Illinois Stretch Energy Code.
rfis.answer: Please provide supporting analysis and summary letter for review. Please confirm the Design-Build Team is taking into account all provisions in the code for laboratories and facilities connecting to central systems such as this one. The State's EnergySense Resilience Center is available to the Design-Build Teams to help them do so: (1) energycode@illinois.edu is the general help line (2) Ryan Siegel (rwsiegel@illinois.edu) has some familiarity with the project

rfis.question: UIC Building Guidelines and Standards Section 33 63 20 Utility Guidelines and Standards - Steam references Sections 33 63 00 Steam Energy Distribution and 40 05 23 Common Work Results for Steam Energy Systems (Non-Buried). Sections 33 63 00 and 40 05 23 are not available on the UIC website. Please provide these two sections.
rfis.answer: Sections 33 63 00 and 40 0523 are in progress and will be available on the UIC website shortly. Please refer to Division 23 for steam / hot water / chilled water requirements within the building.

rfis.question: Please confirm that the proprietary meeting #3 with the Owner can be rescheduled for September 14, 2026 or September 30th, 2026 and advise which.
rfis.answer: Proprietary meeting #3 is scheduled for September 30, 2026.

rfis.question: Per section 4.3 of the Bridging Documents, please confirm that the reference to the Capital Development Board Design and Construction Manual (DCM) should be revised to reference the Standard Documents for Design-Build Projects August 2007 per 00 21 16 - 5.D of the Request for Proposals (RFP)
rfis.answer: The RFP references both the Design and Construction Manual (DCM) and the Standard Documents for Design-Build Projects (SD-DB). The reference to the DCM in the Bridging Documents will remain, and the SD-DB documents stand as listed in the RFP.

rfis.question: Ref: Pg 300-303 of the Bridging Documents. Please provide the following additional documents related to the MV electrical site work:1. Library of Health Sciences (942) b. Administrative Office Building (941) c. Clinical Science Building (920) d. College of Pharmacy Building (924)3. The campus electrical MV primary power one-line diagram.
rfis.answer: 1. Clean copy of the campus electrical site plan with no markups - Please see Attachment 01.

rfis.question: Please provide structural details of the existing Utility Tressle and the other roof areas that will have the new Steam/Condensate and CHWS/R piping so the existing structures can be evaluated.
rfis.answer: This is information is not available. The Design-Build team will be responsible for this independent structural analysis.

rfis.question: To ensure a proposal submission which is compliant with RFP requirements, we request consideration of the following issues as further detailed in the attached letter of concern from our surety who will issue payment and performance bonds for the project: 1. Liquidated Damages - we request implementation of the liquidated damages provision referenced in the Standard Documents for Design-Build Projects General Conditions in a reasonable amount as the sole and exclusive remedy for delay in meeting the required completion date. 2. Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages - we request the incorporation of an industry standard Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages.
rfis.answer: CDB does not intend to implement liquidated damages on this project. Additionally, CDB will not waive any damages allowed by law, including any damages that could be classified as consequential.

rfis.answer: The project was registered on April 15, 2026 as a LEED v4 BD+C: New Construction project.

rfis.question: Can you please clarify/define what "General work" includes in reference to item H on page 1, section 1. For example, would designers performing general work such as lighting or acoustics need to be pre-qualified with CDB? Some designers are registered with CDB as "vendor" but are not necessarily "pre-qualified."
rfis.answer: The designers, performing licensed design services, and all major contractors/subcontractors performing any of the General, Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, and Electrical work must be prequalified with CDB, as an A/E or contractor, before the Phase I submittal deadline. CDB does not prequalify the DB entity separately. Prequalification as a Construction Manager is not acceptable.

rfis.question: For the evaluation of the MBE/WBE/VBE/PBE Goals are the percentage under or over the goals in aggregate for both the MBE/WBE bucker and the VBE/PBE bucket, or are they treated separately. For example, the Design Team Goals are 20% and 3%, would we get credit for exceeding 23% by 25% or more with the excess in one of the two buckets, or do we get the credit if we exceed both the 20% and the 3% separately?
rfis.answer: The total design goal is 23% and the scoring evaluation will be in aggregate.

rfis.question: On the pre-bid call it was mentioned that the design team goal is 20% MBE / 5% WBE. Can you please clarify if there is a VBE requirement for the Design Team?
rfis.answer: The CDB Design Goal is 3% to veteran-owned and/or persons with disability owned businesses. See Page 12 of the RFP for detailed information regarding participation goals for this project.

rfis.question: Would it be possible for you to share the attendee list from the pre-proposal meeting that was held today?
rfis.answer: The attendee list has been posted the project website.

rfis.question: We are a flooring contractor located in Dixon, IL and are interested in bidding for RFP D/B - Construct Northern Illinois Center for Community Sustainability Project. If you are the rep who is dealing with this project could you please share with us the ITB and the bid docs (Flooring package). If not, Can I please have the email of the person who is handling this project?
rfis.answer: The project manager is Kenneth.Watkins@Illinois.gov.

rfis.question: For the evaluation of the MBE/WBE/VBE/PBE Goals, is there a requirement for the VBE/PBE category as there appears to be for the MBE/WBE category, based on the phrase "some level of participation from both MBE and WBE firms is required to satisfy the 20% goal"
rfis.answer: No, the 3% design requirement can be met with either a VBE or a PBE.

rfis.question: On the Phase 1 Utilization Plan Goals Section, there is a statement that the goals 20% and 3% are of the amount of the contract awarded by CDB. Is this a percentage of the entire construction contract, in this case $15m, or a percentage of the A/E design fees or a percentage of a combination of A/E firms and Construction Firms, in which case the 20% and 3% could consist of both A/E firms and Construction Suppliers or Contractors?
rfis.answer: The 20% and 3% are only related to the A/E design portion and not related to any construction costs.

rfis.question: Do we need to submit form 330?
rfis.answer: No. The contents required for Phase I submittal can be found in the RFP under SECTION 00 42 10 – SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS AND INSTRUCTIONS.

rfis.question: Does the DBQ count towards the page count of Section 2?
rfis.answer: Yes.

rfis.question: What contributes to the page count of Section 2?
rfis.answer: It includes the offeror’s Design-Build Entity Qualifications Form (DBQ) and any discussion and or additional information, awards, letters, etc. concerning past performance the offeror includes.

rfis.question: What are the page count limits for Section 1 and Section 4, respectively?
rfis.answer: There are no page limits for section 1. Section 2, 3 and 4 has a combined page limit of 50 pages. Section 2 has a 25 pages limit. Section 3 has a 12 pages total limit with 5 pages limit for technical capacity, 5 pages limit for team experience narrative and 2 pages limit for other capability information.

rfis.question: The purpose in writing was to inquire whether the pre-bid conference that was held on the 29th was recorded, or not. If so, I would like to replay the meeting for our review. Not sure if an attendance sheet was recorded but would also be interested in seeing who else was in the room.
rfis.answer: The recording has been posted to the project website.

rfis.question: During Phase II, will the unselected firms retain ownership of their work product?
rfis.answer: The Design-Build Act states that the drawings and specifications of the proposal shall remain the property of the design-build entity.

rfis.question: When will the pre-bid PowerPoint file be shared?
rfis.answer: It has been posted to the project website.

rfis.question: Is there a way for subconsultants to submit Financial Disclosures and Conflicts of Interest Forms (containing confidential information) directly to the State vs. sending it to various architectural firms to handle? This information looks very similar to what is asked via the CDB and IPG prequalification criteria. Do we still submit this if we are prequalified?
rfis.answer: Financial Disclosures and Conflicts of Interest forms must be included in the submittal. Failure to include these documents for firms listed on the DB-PTF is a material deficiency that may result in rejection of the entire proposal.

rfis.question: Do the General Documents Section forms count towards page count, or no, because they are requested under separate cover?
rfis.answer: No. There are no page limits for section 1.

rfis.question: Please advise if a design consultant to the listed Architect of Record is required to be prequalified prior to the RFP Phase I due date. We won’t be listing them in the DB-PTF, however, they will be listed in our Phase I Utilization plan as well as possibly in DB Qualifications.
rfis.answer: It depends upon the services the consultant will be providing to the AOR. Per the RFP: "The designers, performing licensed design services, and all major contractors/subcontractors performing any of the General, Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, and Electrical work must be prequalified with CDB, as an A/E or contractor, before the Phase I submittal deadline." If they are not providing these licensed services, then they do not need to be prequalified with CDB before the Phase I due date. They will need to get registered with CDB as soon as possible.

rfis.question: Amendment 4 did not have an updated Room Data Sheet for the High Bay Space. Can you provide it? (ASK-10 was uploaded twice)
rfis.answer: This has been updated. 2.. With all the room modifications, it would be helpful to have an updated Spaces Summary Sheet. Can you provide one? And can you clarify if that Summary of Spaces is usable or gross? A. An updated Spaces Summary Sheet will be provided in Amendment 5.

rfis.question: In a previous RFI you mentioned the classroom does not need additional storage, can you provide an updated Room Data Sheet for the “Connected Classrooms”?
rfis.answer: An updated classroom data sheet will be provided in Amendment 5.

rfis.question: The Bridging documents list that the Instrumentation lab contains humidity sensitive equipment, but HVAC basis of design conditions for lab spaces do not include a winter humidity requirement. Is maintaining a year-round minimum humidity level required for instrumentation or other labs? If so, what is the requirement?
rfis.answer: Humidity ranges for specific lab equipment are listed in the cut sheets. Ensure that the HVAC systems can maintain the minimum and maximum humidity ranges for the lab spaces during occupied and non-occupied hours.

rfis.question: Can you provide some background on why the budget changed a second time?
rfis.answer: In calculating the "originally published" budget CDB failed to take into consideration all of the soft costs that had already been committed to. Then when we subsequently increased the funding by Amendment, we failed to realize the original budget error. Once this was identified we "re-adjusted" the budget to what we have now.

rfis.question: Is there a scope change to go along with the new budget?
rfis.answer: The scope of work has not changed.

rfis.question: Are there additional funds outside of the CDB provided funds for the project? And if so, are alternates expected to be proposed?
rfis.answer: There is no additional funding anticipated for this project at this time. There will be no alternate bids.

rfis.question: Confirm that all design documents need to be submitted as 8 ½ x 11 documents.
rfis.answer: The submission is a digital file. Document format size is not limited to 8 1/2 x 11.

rfis.question: Does NIU have any prescribed air change rates for laboratory spaces?
